title: Data-informed priors without double-dipping
text: prior N(β̂,SE2)N(\hat\beta, \mathrm{SE}^2) likelihood approximately N(β̂,SE2)N(\hat\beta, \mathrm{SE}^2), posterior approximately N(β̂,SE2/2)N(\hat\beta, \mathrm{SE}^2/2): data used twice, posterior claims twice information data contain. Credible intervals narrow factor 2\sqrt{2}. quick simulation, using normal approximation posterior, shows consequence coverage nominal 95% intervals: Centring tight prior data drops coverage “95%” intervals 82%, unit-information prior, described next, well calibrated likelihood alone.
code: set.seed(1) n <- 50 sims <- replicate(4000, {   x <- rnorm(n)   y <- 1 + 0.5 * x + rnorm(n)   est <- summary(lm(y ~ x))$coefficients["x", ]   b <- est[[1]]; se <- est[[2]]   post_sd <- c(     flat             = se,                                # likelihood only     same_data_prior  = se / sqrt(2),                      # N(b, se^2) prior, bmbeR 1.x     unit_information = se * sqrt(n / (n + 1))             # N(b, n se^2) prior   )   abs(b - 0.5) <= 1.96 * post_sd }) coverage <- rowMeans(sims) round(coverage, 3) #>             flat  same_data_prior unit_information  #>            0.941            0.821            0.937

code: library(bmbeR) options(mc.cores = 4)                      # run chains in parallel data(kidiq, package = "rstanarm")          # children's test scores train <- kidiq[1:334, ] test  <- kidiq[335:434, ]  # 1. Specify priors in the units of the data priors <- prior_config(   intercept = prior_spec("normal", location = 100, scale = 20),   # at predictor means   slope     = prior_spec("normal", location = 0, scale = c(1, 10)),   aux       = prior_spec("exponential", rate = 1 / 15) )  # 2. Check what the priors imply before seeing the outcome pc <- prior_predictive_check(train, kid_score ~ mom_iq + mom_hs, prior_config = priors,                              plausible_range = c(0, 200))  # 3. Fit; convergence is checked automatically (R-hat, bulk/tail-ESS, divergences, E-BFMI) fit <- fit_model_with_prior(train, kid_score ~ mom_iq + mom_hs, prior_config = priors)  # 4. How much did the prior matter? (power-scaling; no refitting) prior_sensitivity(fit) plot_prior_posterior(fit)  # 5. Score predictions with proper scoring rules perf <- evaluate_model_performance(fit, test)  # 6. Assemble a reporting checklist (Bayesian Analysis Reporting Guidelines) workflow_report(fit, prior_check = pc, performance = perf)

title: Prior and likelihood sensitivity by power-scaling — prior_sensitivity
text: Local sensitivity. derivative posterior expectation respect log(alpha) alpha = 1 equals posterior covariance (Giordano et al., 2018). parameter \(\theta\) posterior mean \(\mu\) standard deviation \(\sigma\), bmbeR reports prior_mean_sens = \(Cov(\theta, \log p(\theta)) / \sigma\): many posterior SDs mean moves per unit change log(alpha); prior_sd_sens = \(Cov((\theta-\mu)^2, \log p(\theta)) / (2\sigma^2)\): relative change posterior SD; lik_mean_sens, lik_sd_sens: log-likelihood. conjugate normal model prior \(N(m_0, s_0^2)\) likelihood \(N(\bar y, s^2)\), -2 * prior_sd_sens share posterior precision contributed prior, -2 * lik_sd_sens share contributed data, conflict_z = prior_mean_sens / (2 * sqrt(prior_sd_sens * lik_sd_sens)) equals \((m_0 - \bar y)/\sqrt{s_0^2 + s^2}\), classic prior predictive check prior-data conflict (Box, 1980). Outside model approximations. See "Prior sensitivity" article package website derivations. Diagnosis (per parameter). prior's influence max(|prior_mean_sens|, |prior_sd_sens|): prior matters moves posterior mean adds precision. likelihood's informativeness |lik_sd_sens|. (lik_mean_sens reported used: symmetric posterior, tempering prior likelihood together leaves mean unchanged, lik_mean_sens = -prior_mean_sens.) "-": prior's influence threshold; likelihood dominates. "weak likelihood": prior influential likelihood informative; data say little parameter. "prior-data conflict": prior influential, likelihood informative, |conflict_z| >= z_threshold; prior data disagree. "informative prior": prior influential likelihood informative, agree; fine prior justified. refines diagnosis Kallioinen et al. (2023), flags potential conflict whenever prior likelihood sensitivity high, separating informative--compatible priors conflicting ones. Finite perturbations. value alpha, posterior power-scaled prior (likelihood) approximated Pareto-smoothed importance sampling (Vehtari et al., 2024). Pareto \(\hat{k}\) diagnostic indicates whether approximation reliable. Weakening (alpha < 1) harder direction: approximately normal posterior importance weights Pareto tail \(k \approx 1 - \alpha\) heavier, values much 0.8 often unreliable. Use sensitivity_analysis() assess large perturbations refitting. Posterior contraction \(1 - \sigma^2_{post}/\sigma^2_{prior}\) (Schad et al., 2021): values near 0 mean data barely updated prior. NA prior variance infinite (flat, Cauchy, Student-t df <= 2). intercept analysed predictor means, parameter rstanarm places prior . Supported: models rstanarm::stan_glm() normal, Student-t, Cauchy, Laplace, flat exponential priors, fitted without QR = TRUE.
